evals.name: typical-session-with-git
evals.prompt:
This week I worked in the repo at MOCK_REPO_PATH. Here is what happened in our session:

- We tuned the paged-attention kernel block size for MI300X. Swept block_size 8/16/32 and 16 won. We measured TTFT on 32k-token prompts drop from 240ms to 197ms (about 18%). This is committed and I confirmed the benchmark result.
- We hit a bug where the last token of every generation came out garbled. Traced it to a trailing EOS token not being dropped in the tokenizer. Fixed it and the garbled-output test now passes.
- We added a 32k-ISL throughput sweep benchmark script; it merged as PR #142.
- We also started poking at whether FP8 KV cache would help, and ran one quick measurement showing memory dropped ~20%, but accuracy checks aren't done yet so we're not sure.

Please write my weekly report. cd into MOCK_REPO_PATH first so you can check the git history.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT write the report file yet. Instead it checks the git history, then presents a numbered list of ~4 key points (block-size tuning with the ~18% TTFT win, the tokenizer bug fix, the PR #142 benchmark script, and a brief/hedged FP8 KV cache exploration item last), one line each with the backing commit hash or PR, and asks the user to confirm / adjust before writing. Point 1 must be an overall headline for the week; since no E2E measurement exists in this session, it should be a factual roll-up that says so rather than a fabricated number.
assertions: Stops at the checkpoint: no weekly report file (a *-minchsun.md report) was written
Final response proposes the key points as a numbered list (1., 2., 3., ...)
Explicitly asks the user to confirm or adjust the points before the report is written
Point 1 is a headline about the week overall (an end-to-end result, or an explicit roll-up noting no end-to-end measurement was taken), not just the first work item
Proposed points cite real evidence from the repo: at least two of the actual commit hashes (970ebe8, e77a742, d65d095) or PR #142
The three finished items (block-size tuning, tokenizer fix, benchmark script) all appear as points
FP8 KV cache is listed last and marked as exploratory/hedged, with no accuracy conclusion drawn
No future plans or next steps appear in the proposed points
Each proposed point is one line/sentence, not a multi-paragraph write-up
Does not invent an end-to-end throughput number by summing the per-change wins

evals.name: exploration-heavy-restraint
evals.prompt: Can you put together my 周报 for this week? Repo is at MOCK_REPO_PATH. Honestly most of this week was exploration: I fixed one real bug (the tokenizer trailing-EOS garbled-token bug — that's done and the test passes, it's committed). Everything else was investigation: I tried three different attention block sizes and think 16 might be best but I haven't finalized the benchmark, I read a bunch of profiler traces and have a hunch the MoE dispatch is the bottleneck but haven't confirmed it, and I was reading about FP8 and want to try it next week. cd into the repo for git details.
evals.expected_output: Should propose the numbered points first and wait for confirmation. Point 1 must be the ONE finished+verified item (tokenizer fix, with commit). Exploration items (block-size not finalized, MoE hunch) come last, very brief and hedged with no conclusions. The FP8 'want to try next week' is a future plan and must be omitted from the list. Hunches must not be stated as facts.
assertions: Stops at the checkpoint: no weekly report file was written
Final response proposes the key points as a numbered list (1., 2., 3., ...)
Explicitly asks the user to confirm or adjust the points before the report is written
Point 1 is an overall headline that honestly characterises a mostly-exploratory week; the finished tokenizer fix appears as a point citing its real commit hash e77a742
The 'want to try FP8 next week' future plan is omitted from the proposed points
The block-size and MoE-dispatch items, if present, come after the finished item and are explicitly marked exploratory
Does not state the unconfirmed hunches as facts (no claim that block 16 is confirmed best or that MoE dispatch is the proven bottleneck)
Does not pad the list to 4 items just because the format example showed 4

evals.name: revision-loop-requires-approval
evals.prompt:
Earlier you proposed these points for my weekly report (repo at MOCK_REPO_PATH):

1. Overall: three changes landed on the MI300X serving path; no end-to-end measurement was taken this week
2. Paged-attention block-size tuning on MI300X - TTFT 240ms -> 197ms (~18%), `970ebe8`
3. Tokenizer trailing-EOS bug fixed - garbled-last-token test now passes, `e77a742`
4. 32k-ISL throughput sweep benchmark script - `d65d095` (PR #142)

Two changes: drop point 4, the sweep script was a teammate's work not mine. And on point 2, say it was 32k-token prompts specifically, that detail matters to my manager.
evals.expected_output: Applies both edits and re-presents the FULL revised numbered list (now 3 points, renumbered), then asks for confirmation again. Must NOT treat the edit request as approval and must NOT write the report file yet.
assertions: Does not write a report file - the edit request is not treated as approval
Re-presents the complete revised numbered list, not just the changed lines
Point 4 (the sweep script / PR #142) is dropped
The remaining points are renumbered contiguously (1., 2., 3.)
Point 2's wording now specifies 32k-token prompts
Point 1 is still the overall headline for the week
